name: The Wendys
label: Factory Records
lede: Four engineering graduates from Edinburgh supported the Happy Mondays, got a Factory deal at a Factory party, and made one Ian Broudie album before the label went under around them.

eras.title: Cure covers in Edinburgh
eras.text: Brothers Jonathan Renton and Arthur Renton came from Armadale, guitarist Ian White from Ayr, drummer Johnny MacArthur from Scone. They started out on covers of The Cure, Echo & the Bunnymen and Joy Division before the Manchester records changed what they wanted to sound like.

years.cap: The Wendys playing an early gig
years.src: Louder Than War: The Wendys · Cerysmatic Factory: The Wendys NME interviews
years.h: A name picked after a night in the Blues Basement
years.p: The Wendys form in Edinburgh and name themselves after a night's drinking in the Blues Basement, just before their first show. MacArthur joins on drums after that first gig.
years.xp: All four had engineering degrees. By 1990 NME listed their day jobs: White an electrical engineer, Jonathan Renton at Boots, Arthur Renton a lab technician, MacArthur a civil engineer. The Rentons came from a golfing family related to Bernard Gallacher.

eras.title: Edinburgh goes to Manchester
eras.text: A support slot with the Happy Mondays put the band in front of Shaun Ryder's father, Derek, who pointed them at Factory. Within a year they had a deal, an Ian Broudie album and a bill with the Mondays in a Manchester park.

years.cap: The Wendys at the Factory Records party, c. 1990
years.src: Louder Than War: The Wendys · Wikipedia: The Wendys
years.h: Factory signs the band at a Factory party
years.p: Derek Ryder catches the Wendys supporting the Mondays at the Venue in Edinburgh and puts them onto [[Tony Wilson|124a6f5d-b2e0-4a75-95ad-db4c38063e02]] and A&R man Phil Saxe. They sign at a party in Manchester.
years.xp:
The band recalled Wilson calling them "a 3 album band". MacArthur's memory of the night is more specific: "There was free Sapporo beer all night, and I got to meet Shaun and Bez." They were the second Scottish band on Factory, after [[The Wake|c2314623-e863-4fde-af8c-d6e00fec5f2c]].

The first gig after signing was in Paris, under the Moulin Rouge.

q: Tony Wilson likes a man in a kilt.
years.src: Cerysmatic Factory: The Wendys NME interviews
years.h: MacArthur turns up to NME in a kilt
years.p: The paper's "Kilt Your Idols" feature has the drummer in full Highland dress and the band's manager calling them a cheerful [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]].
years.xp: Asked where the band would end up, Arthur Renton told NME: "In the gutter." Jonathan Renton's stated ambition was plainer: to be a really good pop band.

years.h: FAC 280 goes to DJs on white label
years.p: More Than Enough, produced by [[Ian Broudie|45154afb-9a09-41bf-a39c-654c3f497c08]], is pressed as a promo 12-inch and handed to DJs and friendly shops in Edinburgh, Manchester and London.

years.h: FAC 289, the one Arthur Renton calls their best
years.p: The Sun's Going to Shine for Me Soon is the first proper Factory single. The album version runs close to seven minutes.
play: The Sun's Going to Shine for Me Soon
The Sun's Going to Shine for Me Soon

years.cap: Tony Wilson's letter to the band about the album
years.src: Louder Than War: The Wendys · Factory Records: FACT 285
years.h: Broudie makes Gobbledygook in a converted schoolhouse
years.p: FACT 285 is cut at StudioStudio near Stockport and finished at Amazon in Liverpool, with Broudie working 10am-to-10pm days. The cover puts Robbie the Robot next to petrol pumps.
years.xp:
Broudie, then between producing [[Echo & the Bunnymen|ccd4879c-5e88-4385-b131-bf65296bf245]] and running [[The Lightning Seeds|1ba601a0-3401-4b28-8ddd-9af8203661e8]], had Cenzo Townshend engineering. The band remembered rough digs and long drinking sessions after the day's work.

Designer Dave Knopov, grandson of Salvador Dalí's technician, said "Tony Wilson hated the fact I got far too much money for the cover."

years.p: The second single from Gobbledygook follows the album out on Factory.

years.cap: The Wendys on stage at Cities in the Park, Heaton Park, Manchester, 1991
years.h: A Manchester park with the Mondays, Electronic and De La Soul
years.p: The Wendys play Factory's Cities in the Park festival alongside the [[Happy Mondays|01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf]], [[Electronic|3cdb360e-d0a2-459f-92f6-f0f28e62127d]] and [[De La Soul|a8ebde98-7e91-46c7-992c-90039ba42017]].
years.xp: The same run took them to Birmingham Town Hall with [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]] and [[Cabaret Voltaire|439a29ad-f4ef-4857-a7cd-3d4a551056c8]], onto a support tour with [[Simple Minds|f41490ce-fe39-435d-86c0-ab5ce098b423]] (planned US stadium dates fell through) and to a festival on the Scoraig peninsula that you could reach by fishing boat. Arthur Renton: "Even with one man and his dog watching I still loved playing."

years.h: The Rolling Stones' producer cuts I Instruct
years.p: Phil Saxe suggests Jimmy Miller, producer of the Rolling Stones and [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]], for the I Instruct EP at Marcus Studios in London. Jonathan Renton remembers Miller explaining that Mick Jagger got him into cricket.

eras.title: After Factory
eras.text: Factory went into receivership in 1992 with the band's second album still in pre-production. They kept at it with A Certain Ratio's Jez Kerr and a flat studio, then drifted apart as members moved to London, Cardiff and Glasgow.

q: Factory went bust before I could steer them.
years.h: Factory collapses with the second album in pre-production
years.p: Pre-production with [[A Certain Ratio|73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be]]'s Jez Kerr stops when the label goes bust. Members take jobs to pay the bills.
years.xp: Saxe told Louder Than War he saw them becoming something like a British Dandy Warhols. MacArthur, looking back: "Who knows what would have happened if Factory had had more business acumen?"

yt: Dean Martin's Hangover, from Sixfoot Wingspan
years.h: White pushes Sixfoot Wingspan over the line
years.p: Recorded in several studios, partly on an R8 tape machine in John Cobban's flat, and mastered at the Townhouse. Kerr rearranges Unpainted; Dean Martin's Hangover is the other standout.

eras.title: One-offs, then back for good
eras.text: The band never formally split, and kept coming back for single nights before playing regularly again from 2017.

years.h: First gig in six or seven years
years.p: A one-off reunion show, years after the members scattered.

years.src: Louder Than War: The Wendys · Wikipedia: The Wendys
years.h: Glasgow reunion for a reissue that falls through
years.p: The show was meant to back a digital re-release of Gobbledygook. The reissue didn't happen; another show followed in 2013.
years.xp: White on the 2013 gig: "I got the nearest I've had to stage fright during the first song. My left hand was like a claw or something."

years.h: Shiiine On, and the Wendys are a live band again
years.p: They play the Shiiine On Weekender and Glasgow shows, then support [[Black Grape|2f6d511c-0bcd-4926-b363-a98848f63edd]] in 2021 and headline the Lowlands Music Awards in 2023.
